pages.text: "One more, one more!" Coco, a little mouse in a red headscarf, stacked bread on the shop floor. The tower was already as tall as Coco. On tiptoe, Coco added another loaf. "All the way to the ceiling!"
Jingle! Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks, came in, brushing off snow. The end of the sack on his shoulder touched the tower. Crash! Bread rolled across the floor.
"Waaah! My tower!" Coco shouted and stamped their feet. Coco picked up a loaf and threw it toward the door. "Coco, I'm sorry..." Mr. Pig stood in the doorway, not knowing what to do.
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, came out holding a bread paddle. Steam curled from fresh bread on it. "Coco, does your face feel as hot as this bread?" Mom sat beside Coco.
Coco held both cheeks and nodded. "Hot..." Mom blew on the bread. "See? The steam settles. Anger is the same. When you feel hot, blow as if cooling bread."
Coco blew at the bread too. Whoo, whoo, whoo—three times. The steam settled, and Coco's face cooled. "Oh? I feel cool! Angry? Blow like cooling bread!"
Coco pulled the headscarf knot tight with both front paws, then walked to Mr. Pig at the door. "I'm sorry I threw the bread." "I'm sorry too, Coco." He grinned wide.
They stacked the bread again. Mr. Pig did the high parts. The tower grew taller than before, and Coco leaned their head right back. "Wow! It could reach the ceiling!" Coco clapped.
Now, when Coco felt angry, they did this. "One, say, 'I feel hot!' Two, blow three times! Three, then talk!" That evening, when the bread basket tipped over, Coco blew. Whoo, whoo, whoo.
Mom hugged Coco in her floury arms. "Anger is like hot bread. Blow on it, and it becomes soft again." Coco smiled in Mom's arms. "Angry? Blow like cooling bread!"
